text: Theo provisions the primary AKS cluster in East US 2, a region with three availability zones, spreading both the system node pool and a dedicated application node pool across all three with the zones flag and a cluster autoscaler ranging from 3 to 15 nodes.

checkout-api's Deployment gets real resource requests and limits, a readiness probe, and a HorizontalPodAutoscaler that scales it from 6 to 30 replicas on CPU utilization. Against most checklists, that's a solid, production-shaped Deployment.

But read the manifest's pod spec again: there's no topologySpreadConstraints, no podAntiAffinity. Nothing tells the scheduler where, relative to other checkout-api pods, a new pod should land — it's free to concentrate several pods onto nodes in the very same availability zone.

At today's low replica counts, on a freshly built, evenly empty node pool, that gap doesn't show up at all — placement just happens to look even. It takes a fast scale-out under genuinely uneven real traffic for it to matter, which is exactly what this capstone comes back to starting in Lesson 10.
